title: Gentle prefetch shepherd: windowed admission adapter for starvation prevention
author: Maya Chen
commits: a1b2c3d: introduce soft-prefetch-credit type and basic bookkeeping
b2c3d4e: implement windowed admission adapter with decay passthrough
c3d4e5f: kernel affinity hints for dispatcher to prefer quantized kernels
d4e5f6a: KV pin gentle-evict hook and backoff integration
e5f6a7b: add unit + integration tests and microbench harness
description: Context: High tail latency for small, KV-heavy requests in continuous batching clusters under sustained load. Motivation: Prior admission controls were aggressive and caused live requests to starve when KV pins and kernel warmup skewed the batch composition. This PR introduces a 'gentle prefetch shepherd'—a windowed admission adapter that gives transient, decaying prefetch credits to flows that would otherwise starve, while preserving global fairness and latency SLOs. Summary of changes: 1) new windowed admission adapter (pkg/batcher/windowed_adapter.go) that allocates a small, time-bounded prefetch budget to low-progress flows; the budget decays exponentially and is charged against a soft-reservation counter to prevent abuse. 2) prefetch_shepherd scheduler component (pkg/scheduler/prefetch_shepherd.go) that tracks per-flow progress, KV-pin state, recent kernel misses, and signals the adapter when to issue credits. 3) kernel affinity hints (runtime/kernel_affinity.go) so dispatcher prefers quantized/fast kernels for shepherded slots to minimize additional warmup cost. 4) KV gentle-evict hook (pkg/kv/pin_manager.go) which tolerates short-lived pins from shepherded slots and schedules cooperative evictions rather than hard drops. 5) tests and microbench harness additions (tests/integration/prefetch_shepherd_test.go, benchmarks/prefetch_shepherd_microbench.json). Design notes: The adapter keeps a sliding window per-cohort instead of strict per-request leases; this reduces jitter and makes admission decisions smoother under bursts. Credits are small (configurable default 2 tokens) and decay with an exponential half-life to avoid long-term priority inversion. The prefetch shepherd observes kernel-warmup events and will not issue credits that would force the dispatcher to run a cold heavy kernel if a warm fast kernel is available for alternatives. Safety and fairness: We added global credit caps, cohort-weight-aware decay, and a backoff on repeated credits to avoid gaming. The admission path includes instrumentation to report credit issuance, decay events, and credit exhaustion to the Console so operators can tune policy. Benchmarks: Microbench runs show median token latency unchanged, 95th reduced by ~8-12% on KV-heavy small-request workloads, and P99 down ~6% under sustained 90% load with mixed kernel types. CPU/GPU overhead measured at infra-level is <1.5% in steady state. Backwards compatibility: configuration defaults disable shepherding for Dedicated private installs until customer opt-in; the feature is off by default for older clusters. Review notes: Addressed concerns about priority inversion by adding cohort-weight-aware decay and global caps; added an E2E test that simulates long-lived KV-pin churn. Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-4882) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Benchmarks recorded - [x] Feature gated and rollout plan documented in docs/operational/continuous-batcher-tuning.md Commits summary: a1b2c3d: introduce soft-prefetch-credit type and basic bookkeeping; b2c3d4e: implement windowed admission adapter with decay passthrough; c3d4e5f: kernel affinity hints for dispatcher to prefer quantized kernels; d4e5f6a: KV pin gentle-evict hook and backoff integration; e5f6a7b: add unit + integration tests and microbench harness. Files changed at a glance: windowed_adapter.go (core logic + config knobs), prefetch_shepherd.go (cohort tracking + heuristic signals), kernel_affinity.go (dispatcher hints), pin_manager.go (gentle eviction), integration test harness, docs and benchmark artifacts. Review conversation snapshot: Aaron Patel: "Initial read looks solid; main worry is credit leakage in pathological churn. Can you add an explicit drain path at flow termination?" Maya Chen: "Added drain in d4e5f6a; adapter closes outstanding credits on flow end and reports metrics." Sofia Martinez: "Please ensure we expose a per-tenant cap; ops will want to throttle on multi-tenant hosts." Maya Chen: "Added per-tenant cap and config, default conservative; docs updated." Eliot James: "Benchmarks look promising; please run perf canary on staging with mixed kernel pool." Maya Chen: "Canary run scheduled and green; CI/bench reports attached." CI: unit tests passed, integration tests passed on staging, perf microbench passed; two flaky lint warnings fixed in follow-up commit. Merge: squashed and merged into main after reviewer approvals. Operational notes for SRE: Watch for rapid credit churn metric (batcher.prefetch.credit_churn) and credit_exhaustion alarms; default alert thresholds provided in docs. Rollout plan: feature flagged, enable in canary cluster for 48h, monitor P95/P99 and credit churn, then ramp 10/30/100%. Why this is different: instead of preemptive hard reservations or aggressive deadline relaxations, this approach uses a small bounded, decaying credit mechanism tied to kernel warmup and KV state to mitigate transient starvation without distorting long-term fairness.
